semester: 5th Semester (Winter Semester start); 6th Semester (Summer Semester start)

learning_outcomes.text: Students are able to solve a complex engineering development task, largely open-ended, as a team project with accompanying coaching.
They are able to perform functional breakdowns and create and maintain robust requirements lists based on textual problem descriptions and their own requirements.
They can methodically generate, combine, and evaluate solution variants, also considering sustainability aspects.
Students can translate solution variants into constructive designs using CAD.
They may have learned additional machine elements and calculation methods according to manufacturer specifications, supplementing MAE1-3.
They can largely organize themselves as a project team and apply simple scheduling/project planning tools (e.g., Gantt chart).

syllabus_topics: Systematic analysis of a complex problem, generation of functional breakdown(s) and requirements list, possibly division into subsystems
Systematic generation of solution variants, comparative evaluations, combination into overall solutions, compatibility and installation space investigations
Constructive designs of eventual subsystems and the overall solution
Selected calculations according to TEM1-3 and MAE1-3 and possibly manufacturer documents
Drawing representations according to drawing standards by hand and/or with CAD, in parts detailed standard-compliant manufacturing documents, parts lists, assembly instructions
Creation of a comprehensible and structured documentation of the entire solution process and a reflection on the team work and the result (comparison with the requirements list!)
teaching_methods: Introductory sessions for the full course
Themed events with participants from multiple groups (if applicable)
assessment_rules: To receive credit points, the module examination must be passed. The grade's weight for the final grade is determined by credit points.
